history.caption: The withheld depreciation on a roof claim sits safe behind an event the homeowner controls.
history.title: roof-claim-withheld-depreciation

style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph, 50mm overhead optic with a razor-sharp focal plane, top-down 90-degree view. A thick, embossed insurance settlement document sits on a matte dark walnut desk, with a partially visible bank check protruding from beneath it. Even diffused daylight casting soft shadows, one document slightly out of alignment to look handled. Muted paper tones, heavy tactile paper stock, generous editorial negative space. No legible text.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, typography, people, hands, UI
rationale: The story turns on regulatory rules, contract riders, and settlement sequences hidden in policy papers. A document flatlay perfectly captures the administrative reality of the split-payment model.
subject: an official insurance settlement document overlapping a partially exposed bank check
core_thesis: A replacement-cost roof claim arrives as two payments, and the hidden second check is only paid on proof the work was done inside a policy-granted window.
core_conflict: Guaranteed replacement value versus the rigid proof-of-work deadline.
